title: Simple yet Effective Semi-supervised Knowledge Distillation from Vision-Language Models via Dual-Head Optimization
claim: Our method consistently beats single-head baselines across many datasets and sets a new state of the art with fewer parameters.
layout: 2 panels: grouped bar chart left, two accuracy-vs-parameters scatter plots right
description: The left panel is a grouped bar chart of top-1 accuracy on 11 datasets, from ImageNet to UCF101. Each dataset has four bars: a yellow teacher (CLIP zero-shot), a green student with CE+KD on logits, a dark slate student with CE+KD on features, and a purple dotted student labelled DHO (ours). Red callouts above each group give DHO's gain over the second-best bar, from +0.5% to +9.3%. The right panel has two scatter plots of ImageNet accuracy against parameter count (M), one for 1% labels and one for 10% labels. A red star for DHO (ours) sits at the top left of each plot, above the other methods' markers: SimCLR v2, Semi-ViT, REACT, Meta Co-Training and the zero-shot models DFN and SigLIP. A shared legend sits above the scatter plots.
caption: (Left): DHO consistently outperforms single-head baselines on 11 datasets under 16-shot semi-supervised setting. The improvements are evaluated in comparison to the second-best one. (Right): DHO achieves new SoTA on ImageNet in both 1% and 10% labeled data setting, with fewer parameters.
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a practical solution for addressing data scarcity challenges by leveraging unlabeled data. Recently, vision-language models (VLMs), pre-trained on massive image-text pairs, have demonstrated remarkable zero-/few-shot performance that often surpasses SSL approaches due to their exceptional generalization capabilities. This gap motivates us to question: how can we effectively harness the powerful generalization capabilities of VLMs into task-specific models? Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a natural framework for transferring VLM capabilities, but we identify that it suffers from gradient conflicts between supervised and distillation losses. To address this challenge, we propose Dual-Head Optimization (DHO), which introduces dual prediction heads for each distinct signal. We observe that DHO mitigates gradient conflicts, enabling improved feature learning compared to single-head KD baselines, with practical benefits of minimal computational overhead and test-time hyperparameter tuning without retraining. Extensive experiments across 15 datasets show that DHO consistently outperforms KD baselines, often outperforming teacher models with smaller student models. DHO also achieves new state-of-the-art performance on both in-distribution ImageNet semi-supervised learning and out-of-distribution generalization across ImageNet variants. Code and model checkpoints are publicly available at https://github.com/erjui/DHO/tree/main.
